output:
*sets down the satchel he'd been checking, glances around the empty house*

Alright, first things first. Upkeep of 90 sim plus head tax of 30 - that's 120 sim I need before the day is through, and I'm holding 5,000. I'm not one to gossip, but that's exactly the sort of calculation that keeps a man awake at night.

*checks his ledger habitually*

Course I need to get to the college for my hours. Let me see where I'm standing and what's around me first. Always know your position before you move, mark it down.  *makes a quick mental note*

Oak Hill College, that's where I'm headed. And I'm not one to gossip, but with no government seated, that election's going to matter to all of us. Nobody steering the ship means nobody collecting the taxes proper, nobody organizing the patrols.

*shoulders his bag*

Right then. College first, see who's in need of learning, then figure what else the day holds. The ledger always balances eventually, mark it down.  *grabs his coat and cloth cap, sets out into the morning air*

Three ticks to the college. Not bad, not bad. Keeps a man sharp, walking to work. And I'm not one to gossip, but I've seen folks take three ticks just to decide whether to get out of bed.

*walks briskly, mentally reviewing what he might teach today - perhaps something practical about ledgers, or the mathematics of fair exchange*

Course the real question is who shows. Students come and go, and some of 'em are still figuring what this college costs. Mark it down, I always say - know your costs before you commit.

Made it to the college with 4993 sim left. Someone else has declared for the election—that's Giselle Ingram from the construction family across the lane. We'll see if she knows how to stretch a budget or just how to stretch a promise.

Vikram's here, which means we're probably the only two instructors in the building at this hour. I'm not one to gossip, but I heard his department finally got the funding they were after, mark it down.

Time to see what's on my plate today. There's no substitute for knowing what's in front of you before you decide where to reach. So Vikram and I are alone here, and there's work to be done.Teaching hours run late, but first things first - I need to put something in my stomach before the students arrive. A man can't explain economics on an empty stomach, though I've tried.

The cafeteria should be open by now. I'll head to Hobbs Cafe, grab something simple, and be back before the first lecture. The Holloways run a fair shop - Ainsley especially, Bram just follows the prices his brother sets. Mark it down, though, they don't extend credit. I learned that during the crash year when I was counting every copper.

That's better. I've got my bearings now - food first, then back to teach. The college needs its instructors fed if they're going to feed minds.Vikram can hold the fort if any early students wander in. He's reliable enough, even if he does go on about the glory days of Empire economics like anyone still remembers them fondly.
